title: Quantum Recurrence Plot Algorithm Based on Quantum Principal Component Analysis
authors: Hanhuai Zhu, Jingjing Huang, Zhi-Xi Wang, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: Recurrence Plot (RP) is a method employed to analyze the periodicity, chaoticity, and nonlinear characteristics of complex systems. Quantum Principal Component Analysis (QPCA), on the other hand, achieves dimensionality reduction of sample data using density matrices based on quantum circuits. We improve the distance threshold function of the recurrence plot algorithm using a density operator conceptually equivalent to the covariance matrix, integrate it with quantum circuits, and thereby develop a Quantum Recurrence Plot (QRP) algorithm. This algorithm achieves ultra-high efficiency in parallel computing, reduces computational costs, and simultaneously upgrades the traditional grayscale recurrence plot to colored heatmaps, enabling a better revelation of the system's dynamical characteristics.
summary: This work introduces a Quantum Recurrence Plot (QRP) algorithm that enhances the analysis of complex system periodicity and chaos. By replacing classical distance thresholding with quantum circuit calculations based on density matrices, QRP achieves superior diagnostic quality and theoretical computational efficiency compared to traditional methods. It shows how quantum computation can accelerate nonlinear time series analysis.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve classical Recurrence Plot (RP) analysis, which characterizes complex system dynamics, by developing a Quantum Recurrence Plot (QRP) algorithm.
main_result: The QRP significantly outperforms classical RP by achieving better visualization (colored heatmaps), higher recurrence point density, and superior quantitative metrics like Determinism due to quantum circuit implementation.
method: It integrates Quantum Principal Component Analysis (QPCA) with the Recurrence Plot framework, using quantum circuits (like Swap Test or QPE) to calculate necessary state correlations via density operators.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to complex dynamical systems represented by time series data reconstructed in a phase space using an embedding dimension. The core mathematical tool involves analyzing the covariance matrix through its associated density operator.
key_observables: Recurrence Rate (RR), Determinism (DET), Average Diagonal Length (L), Entropy (ENTR), and the structure of the recurrence plot itself.
important_parameters: Embedding dimension ($m$), time delay ($	au$), and the quantum circuit complexity scaling ($	ext{O}(\log m)$ vs $	ext{O}(m^2)$).
main_assumptions: The speedup relies on ideal quantum hardware with sufficient coherence times; preprocessing steps like determining embedding dimension remain classical.
figures_summary: Figures compare structural patterns (mutation vs. periodic) and quantitative metrics (RQA) between the classical RP and the proposed QRP, alongside complexity comparisons.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of classical RPs, proposes using quantum methods via density operators derived from covariance matrices, details the implementation using quantum circuits for efficiency gains, and validates the improved diagnostics against real-world time series data.
why_interesting: It demonstrates a concrete application of quantum algorithms (QPE, QPCA) to analyze non-linear dynamics in classical physics problems, showing potential speedups over established numerical methods.
